name: first-word-keeps-leading-space
why: does not skip leading whitespace, so it returns an empty view for "  a b".

name: freq-digits-are-letters
why: treats digits as part of words.

edits.old: bool is_letter(char c) { return (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z'); }
edits.new: bool is_letter(char c) { return (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9'); }

name: freq-forgets-last-word
why: does not count the word that ends the text.

edits.old: if (!word.empty()) ++counts[word];  // the text may end in the middle of a word

name: join-no-reserve
why: correct, but grows the string repeatedly (fails the Fast tier).

edits.old: out.reserve(total);  // one allocation for the whole result

name: join-trailing-separator
why: appends the separator after every part, including the last.

name: tokenize-drops-last-word
why: never emits the word at the very end of the text.

edits.new: if (i > start && i < text.size()) tokens.emplace_back(text.substr(start, i - start));

name: tokenize-erase-from-front
why: correct but quadratic: copies the text and erases from the front for every token.

name: tokenize-splits-only-on-space
why: treats only ' ' as whitespace: tabs and newlines stay inside tokens.

edits.old: bool is_space(char c) { return std::isspace(static_cast<unsigned char>(c)) != 0; }

name: trim-leading-only
why: removes leading whitespace but not trailing.

name: trim-returns-dangling-view
why: copies into a local string and returns a view of it, which is destroyed on return.

edits.old: return s.substr(begin, end - begin);  // a view of the same characters: nothing is copied
edits.new:
std::string copy(s.substr(begin, end - begin));
    return copy;
